Art. 1 – Admission to doctoral programs
1. The Call for applications for admissions to the PhD programmes of Politecnico di Torino for the 42nd
cycle is now open.
2. The available programs are as follows:
▪ Architecture. History and Project (with a curriculum in “Transnational Architectural Models in
a Globalized World,” in partnership with the School of Architecture at Tsinghua University)
▪ Bioengineering and Medical-Surgical Sciences (in partnership with Università degli Studi di
Torino, with a curriculum in partnership with Kansai Medical University)
▪ Design and Technology. People, Environment, Systems
▪ Energetics
▪ Physics
▪ Aerospace Engineering
▪ Chemical Engineering
▪ Civil and Environmental Engineering
▪ Electrical, Electronic, and Communications Engineering (with a curriculum in “Electronic
Devices,” in collaboration with the National Institute of Nuclear Physics)
▪ Management and Production Engineering
▪ Computer and Control Engineering
▪ Mechanical Engineering
▪ Patrimonio architettonico / Architectural Heritage
▪ Materials Science and Technology
▪ Mathematical Sciences
▪ Urban and Regional Development (in partnership with Università degli Studi di Torino)
3. The activation of the programmes is subject to the successful outcome of the accreditation
process by the Ministry of University and Research, in accordance with current regulations.
4. The activation of the inter-university PhD programs (Bioengineering and Medical-Surgical
Sciences; Urban and Regional Development) is also subject to the renewal of the agreements
establishing the programs between Politecnico di Torino and Università degli Studi di Torino,
currently under negotiation.
5. The activation of the curriculum in “Electronic Devices” within the PhD program in “Electrical,
Electronic and Communications Engineering” is also subject to the renewal of the agreement
establishing the programme between Politecnico di Torino and the National Institute for Nuclear
Physics, currently under negotiation.
6. Should the accreditation procedure and/or the renewal of the aforementioned agreements result
in a negative outcome, thereby jeopardizing the activation of the PhD programs and/or of the
above-mentioned curriculum, candidates will be promptly notified via the ticketing support
service referred to in Art. 24.
7. The start of courses at Politecnico di Torino is set for:
▪ 15th September 2026, for successful candidates of the first competition session who meet the
admission requirements set forth in Art. 7 by 31st August 2026;
▪ 1st November 2026, for successful candidates of the first competition session who meet the
admission requirements set forth in Art. 7 by 31st October 2026;
▪ 1st March 2027, for successful candidates of the second competition session;
▪ 1st June 2027, for successful candidates of the third competition session.

8. The competition sessions and the corresponding start dates for the doctoral program are specified
in Art. 6 and Art. 9, par. 1 of this call for applications.
9. The doctoral program lasts 36 months, subject to extensions in accordance with the University’s
current regulations governing doctoral studies.
Art. 2 – Types of Positions Available
1. The positions available are classified as follows:
A) REGULAR POSITIONS
i. Positions with a scholarship and own research topic
These positions are associated with scholarships that do not require a predefined research
topic.
The thesis topic will be agreed upon, after admission, with the Program Coordinator and the
Supervisor.
All applicants are automatically considered for open-topic scholarships, unless they expressly
decline.
ii. Positions with scholarships and predefined research topic
These positions are associated with scholarships that require research to be compulsorily
conducted on a specific topic, as described in the information sheet published on the
institutional website.
Candidates must select the thematic scholarships in accordance with the procedures and
deadlines indicated in Art. 5, par. 1.
iii. Positions offered in apprenticeship format
These positions require both:
▪ enrollment in a doctoral program,
▪ employment with a company under an apprenticeship contract of a duration equivalent
to that of the educational project.
To activate the contract, the candidate must not have reached the age of 30 by the date of
hiring by the company.
The apprenticeship contract entered into pursuant to Art. 45 of Legislative Decree No. 81/2015
terminates upon the attainment of a university degree and/or the completion of the
educational project.
Those interested in this type of position must follow the provisions of Art. 5, par. 1.
iv. Positions without a scholarship
These are positions for which no doctoral scholarship is provided.
Candidates wishing to apply for these positions must follow the provisions of Art. 5, par. 2.
Admission is based on the ranking order among eligible candidates.
B) RESERVED POSITIONS
v. Positions reserved for recipients of scholarships awarded by foreign governments
These positions are reserved for candidates who already hold a scholarship awarded by for-
eign countries.
Admission is based on the ranking order among eligible candidates.
vi. Positions with scholarships reserved for the POLITO for REFUGEES project
These are positions reserved for beneficiaries of international protection. The application pro-
cedures are outlined in Annex 1.

vii. Positions reserved for specific international initiatives
These are positions reserved for candidates pre-selected by partner institutions or universities
as part of international collaborations with the University.
Activation is subject to the availability of funding.
The application procedures are outlined in the individual scholarship descriptions.
viii. Positions reserved for research fellows
Positions are awarded, based on ranking, to those who, at the conclusion of the competition,
are eligible for admission and already hold a research fellowship.
The number of spots reserved for research fellows is equal to half the number of regular spots
available for each program, rounded up to the nearest whole number.
The topic of the research fellowship must coincide with that of the doctoral dissertation.
The Academic Board may issue a binding opinion regarding the compatibility of the two ac-
tivities.
Candidates holding a research fellowship participate in the same selection procedure as
other candidates and must meet the eligibility requirements established in this call for appli-
cations.
Art. 3 – Positions available
1. For the 42nd cycle, a minimum of 110 positions with scholarships are being offered.
2. Any additional positions or scholarships that become available after the publication of this call for
applications will be announced via an update published exclusively on the University’s institutional
website.
Updates published on the University’s official website shall constitute official communication for
the purposes of this call for applications.
3. The positions referred to in par. 1 are distributed among the various doctoral programs as follows:

4. The scholarships are distributed across the three application sessions as shown in the table, which
is an integral part of the call for applications and is published on the institutional website.
5. The final list of available positions for each session and each doctoral program will be published
on the designated webpage no later than 6 days prior to the start date of the interviews set by
each Admissions Committee and announced in accordance with the procedures outlined in Art.
14.
Art. 4 – Characteristics and amount of the doctoral scholarship
1. The doctoral scholarship is awarded on an annual basis and is renewed for each academic year,
provided that the student has completed the program of activities required for the previous year
and has been admitted to the next academic year by the Academic Board. The scholarship is
awarded for a maximum of 36 months, subject to the provisions of Art. 36, par. 2, of the Regulations
for doctoral programmes of Politecnico di Torino.
2. The annual amount of the scholarship for the 2026/27 academic year is € 18,854.52, gross of social
security contributions payable by the recipient (net monthly amount of approximately €1,386,
subject to changes in social security rates). The doctoral scholarship is exempt from local income
tax and personal income tax (IRPEF) and is subject to the payment of INPS social security
contributions under a separate fund, with two-thirds paid by Politecnico di Torino and one-third
by the recipient.
3. The scholarship amount is increased proportionally by 50% for any periods spent abroad, in
accordance with current regulations.
4. In addition, a budget for research activities is made available to the doctoral student, equal to
10% of the total cost of the scholarship, to be used over the course of the 36-month period.
5. The following categories of applicants are not eligible for a doctoral scholarship:
a) those who have already received a scholarship for a doctoral program in Italy;
b) public employees on special leave who retain their salary, social security, and pension
benefits;
c) holders of a Higher Education and Research apprenticeship contract (Art. 45 of Legislative
Decree No. 81/2015);
d) research fellows (see Art. 2, para. 1, letter b);
e) holders of research positions (Art. 22-ter of Law No. 240 of December 30, 2010).
Art. 5 – Selection or waiver of positions with thematically restricted scholarships and apprenticeship
positions
1. Candidates interested in applying for positions with predefined research topic and/or for positions
in apprenticeship format must:
▪ carefully read the scholarship description, which specifies the topic and required skills;
▪ if necessary, contact the scientific supervisor indicated in the description;
▪ select up to a maximum of 5 options via the online Apply procedure (see Art. 9).
Selection may be made starting 5 days before the start date of the interviews for the relevant
doctoral program and no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon – CET time) on the day before the

interviews begin. Please note that the start date of the interviews is set by each Admissions
Committee and announced in accordance with the procedures set forth in Art. 14.
2. Candidates who intend to participate in the competition while waiving all scholarships (whether
with own research topic or predefined research topic) or apprenticeship positions must submit
their waiver via the online Apply procedure (see Art. 9) starting 5 days before the start date of the
interviews for the relevant doctoral program and no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon – CET time) on the
day preceding the start of those interviews. The option exercised is irrevocable.
3. It is understood that if no positions without a scholarship are available for the doctoral program of
interest, the withdrawal from all scholarships or apprenticeship positions will result in exclusion from
the competition, with the exception of any surplus positions reserved for research fellows.
Art. 6 – Selection sessions
1. The selection process for admission to the 42nd cycle doctoral programs is divided into three
distinct and independent sessions, hereinafter referred to as the “first session,” “second session,”
and “third session.”
2. It should be noted that each competition session has its own evaluation process, which is
completed within that session and therefore generates independent rankings across the different
sessions.
Art. 7 – Admission requirements for the selection process
1. Italian and foreign citizens who, as of the deadline set for each session (see Art. 9, para. 1), meet
the following requirements may apply to participate in the selection process.
2. Applicants with a second-level degree obtained in Italy
a) Master’s degree, specialized degree, or bachelor’s degree awarded under the regulations in
effect prior to Ministerial Decree No. 509 of November 3, 1999, as amended by Ministerial
Decree No. 270 of October 22, 2004;
b) Minimum grade of 95/110;
c) Certification of English language proficiency at the B2 level (as defined by the Common
European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR)), among those listed in Annex 4 of
this call for applications, regardless of the date of issuance. Certifications other than those
listed in Annex 4 will not be considered.
Cases of exemption are indicated in Annex 3.
2.1. Those who, by the application deadline (see Art. 9, para. 1), do not yet hold a Level II degree
and/or language certification may also participate in the competition “conditionally.” With
regard to the Level II degree, candidates must have a weighted average of at least 25/30
on the exams taken.
2.2. Those admitted to the competition “conditionally” must, in any case, obtain the degree and
language certification by the following dates:
▪ 31st August 2026, or 31st October 2026, for the first session;
▪ 15th February 2027, for the second session;
▪ 15th May 2027, for the third session.
2.3. The second-level degree must, in any case, be obtained with a minimum grade of 95/110.

2.4. Failure to obtain the degree by the dates indicated above and with the required minimum
grade will result in exclusion from the competition.
3. Candidates with a second-level degree obtained abroad
a) A second-level academic degree under the Bologna Process or a Master’s degree that grants
access to doctoral studies in the country of origin (EQF Level 8), issued by an officially
recognized or accredited institution;
b) Minimum grade point average for exams taken as indicated in Annex 2;
c) Certification of English language proficiency at level B2 (as defined by the Common European
Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), among those listed in Annex 4 of this call for
applications, regardless of the date of issuance. Certifications other than those listed in Annex
4 will not be considered.
Cases of exemption are indicated in Annex 3.
3.1. The eligibility of academic qualifications obtained abroad is assessed, solely for the purposes
of admission to the competition for the 42nd cycle, by the Commission referred to in Art. 12
based on the documentation attached to the application for admission to the competition
referred to in Art. 8.
3.2. Those who, by the application deadline (see Art. 9, para. 1), have not yet obtained their
academic degree and/or language certification may also participate in the competition
“conditionally.” Regarding the master’s degree, candidates must have a minimum grade
point average on the exams taken as indicated in Annex 2;
3.3. In such cases, the degree and certification must be obtained by the following dates:
▪ 31st August 2026, or 31st October 2026, for the first session;
▪ 15th February 2027, for the second session;
▪ 15th May 2027, for the third session.
3.4 Failure to obtain the degree by the dates specified above and with the minimum grades
specified above will result in exclusion from the competition.
Art. 8 – Application documentation
1. The applicant must upload the following required documents in the Apply procedure:
a) Identification document
Front and back copies of a valid ID document with photo and signature.
b) Bachelor’s degree
If obtained in Italy:
You must upload your complete study plan to the “Educational background” section of Apply
with the date and final grade of the degree.
If obtained abroad:
i. Bachelor’s degree (EQF Level 6) corresponding to the Italian Laurea qualification, issued by an
accredited/recognized foreign university and granting access to master’s programs (EQF Level
7). Certified Copies, Certified True Copies, and Attested Copies are also accepted.
ii. A complete transcript of records, scanned front and back, listing all exams taken with grades
and credits earned.
c) Master’s degree
If already obtained at the time of application and issued by an Italian institution:

Enter the complete study plan in the “Educational background” section of Apply, along with the
date and final grade of the degree obtained.
If not yet obtained at the time of application at an Italian institution:
It is necessary to upload the study plan in the “Education background” section of Apply, includ-
ing the exams taken up to the date of application submission.
If already obtained at the time of application and issued by a foreign institution:
iii. Master’s degree (EQF Level 7) equivalent to the Italian Laurea Magistrale qualification, issued by
an accredited/recognized foreign university and granting access to doctoral studies in the coun-
try of origin (EQF Level 8). Certified copies, Certified True Copies, and Attested Copies are also
accepted.
iv. Complete transcript of records, scanned front and back, listing all exams taken with grades and
credits earned.
If not yet obtained at the time of application at a foreign institution:
Most up-to-date transcript of records, scanned front and back, including all exams taken with
the corresponding grades and credits obtained. If you are currently attending your final year,
please attach the most up-to-date transcript available, including the final or provisional GPA.
d) Language certification
Certificate of English language proficiency at the B2 level, if already obtained, exclusively from
those listed in Annex 4.
In the event of an exemption, as provided for in Annex 3, official documentation from the
institution where the program was completed must be uploaded, certifying that the program
was conducted entirely in English, along with the corresponding grade, date, and place of
completion.
e) Abstract of the Master’s thesis
A document in PDF format written in English (3,000–6,000 characters, excluding spaces) must be
uploaded, containing a concise yet comprehensive description of the general objectives,
methodologies used, results achieved, and, above all, the individual contribution. Tables, graphs,
and/or images may be included.
f) Motivational statement
A PDF document written in English (max 8,000 characters, excluding spaces) must be uploaded,
containing a description of your scientific interests and motivations for pursuing the PhD. You must
highlight your objectives, aspirations, and personal aptitude for conducting the scientific
research that will be the focus of the PhD. The statement must also demonstrate the ability to
develop a research project, outlining its premises, objectives, and the methodology to be
followed.
If applying to multiple programs, you may upload a separate statement for each program.
g) Referee
You must provide the names and institutional email addresses of two referees whom the
Admissions Committee may contact regarding the application.
It is preferable to list a faculty member from another university, whether Italian or foreign, and a
faculty member from the Politecnico di Torino. For joint doctoral programs, the name of the
Politecnico faculty member may be replaced by the name of a faculty member or equivalent
from the partner institution. The inclusion of these names does not necessarily imply the submission
of a letter of reference, as referred to in par. 3, letter l).

2. All documents relating to academic qualifications obtained abroad must be:
▪ issued on letterhead, stamped, and signed by the issuing institution, or digitally signed and/or
verifiable online via a QR code or verification link;
▪ written in Italian, English, French, or Spanish. If they are written in other languages, both the

▪ for non-EU qualifications, if this information is not already included in the transcript, an official
statement from the university must be provided describing:
o the grading system (minimum and maximum grades required to pass individual exams);
o any cumulative grade point average (GPA/CGPA);
o the final degree grade;
o the credit system.
3. The applicant may upload the following documents to the Apply portal; while not mandatory,
they are strongly recommended:
h) Declaration of Value or Certificate of Comparability and/or Verification issued by CIMEA – ENIC
NARIC Italia for first- and second-level degrees;
i) Diploma Supplement (DS) for first- and second-level degrees (for degrees awarded in countries
participating in the Bologna Process);
j) An official document indicating the expected date of completion of the foreign degree, if you
are currently in your final year of study.
k) For degrees awarded by the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, China, France, and for
countries where there is a distinction between academic qualifications and vocational qualifica-
tions, please refer to Annex 6.
4. The applicant may upload the following optional documents via the Apply portal:
l) Letters of recommendation from university professors, researchers, or representatives of institutions
or businesses. The names of the signatories of the letters of recommendation may also differ from
the names listed in letter g).
m) GRE score (obtained within the last 5 years);
n) Publications. Information regarding publications (type of publication, authors, date, etc.) may be
entered in the designated section of the Apply procedure;
o) Any other documents deemed useful to support the application (e.g., other first- and second-level
degrees, awards, post-graduate schools, professional experience, other documents relevant to
the statement of eligibility, etc.).
All documents must be included in a single .pdf file to be uploaded in the designated field in the
“Attachments” section of the online Apply procedure;
5. The application to participate in the competition includes all of the aforementioned attachments,
which form an integral part thereof.
6. The application is submitted in the form of a self-certification pursuant to Articles 46 and 47 of
Presidential Decree 445/2000, as amended. The candidate is responsible for the accuracy of the
statements made.

Art. 10 – Candidates with certification of disability, impairment, or a diagnosis of Specific Learning
Disorder (SLD)
1. Candidates who require special arrangements for the interview must submit, within 15 business
days of the interview date, appropriate documentation (attaching it in .pdf format via the Apply
portal). In particular, please note that:
a) those in possession of a disability certificate or a disability certification as referred to in Art. 16
of Law No. 104/92 must submit appropriate certification issued by the competent local
medical commission, attesting to the type of recognized disability and/or the degree of
disability;
b) those who have been diagnosed with specific learning disorders (SLD), as referred to in Law
No. 170/2010, must submit appropriate certification issued no more than 3 years prior (at the
time of enrollment in the bachelor’s degree program) by National Health Service (SSN)
facilities or by specialists and facilities accredited by the SSN. Certifications issued upon
reaching the age of eighteen are also valid;
c) applicants holding a disability certificate or SLD certificate who reside in foreign countries must
submit certification attesting to their disability or SLD status issued in their country of residence.
The documents must be official, bearing the stamp of the issuing institution and the signature
of the authorized official, and must be written in one of the following languages: Italian, English,
French, or Spanish. If the official documents are in other languages, both the original language
version and the official translation into Italian or English must be attached in the same file. The
University authorities responsible for reviewing the certifications referred to in this section shall
verify that the foreign documentation attests to a disability or specific learning disorder
recognized by Italian law.
2. The organization of the interviews referred to in this Call will take these needs into account in
accordance with current regulations, following verification of the certifications by the Special
Needs Unit of Politecnico di Torino, which will validate their suitability.
3. The following compensatory measures are provided for the interview:
a) Additional time (30% extra, which may be increased to 50% for candidates with disabilities
upon explicit request);
b) Use of a calculator;
c) Possibility of having a sign language interpreter present, to be requested within 15 business
days of the interview date, concurrently with the submission of the aforementioned
documentation.
4. For any other needs, contact the Special Needs Unit through the Ticketing Assistance Service.

Art. 11 – Application evaluation process
1. The selection procedure for admission to the PhD programs at Politecnico di Torino consists of the
following stages:
a) verification of admission requirements;
b) evaluation of qualifications, scientific interests, and motivation;
c) interview.
2. The verification of requirements is intended to confirm that the admission conditions specified in
the call for applications are met and constitutes a preliminary and necessary step for the appli-
cation to proceed (see Art. 12).
3. Applications found eligible following the verification of requirements are submitted for evaluation
of qualifications, scientific interests, and motivation by the Admissions Committee appointed for
each doctoral program.
4. Only applicants who have achieved the minimum threshold required in the evaluation of qualifi-
cations, scientific interests, and motivation will be admitted to the interview (see Art. 13).
5. The interview is designed to assess the candidate’s preparation, motivation, and aptitude for re-

Annex 6 – Specific notes regarding the documentation to be attached to the application
We recommend uploading the following non-mandatory documentation, which is strongly advised
for those who already hold a degree, along with other specific notes:
▪ Statement of Value or Certificate of Comparability and/or Verification issued by CIMEA – ENIC
NARIC Italy for first- and second-level degrees;
▪ Diploma Supplement (DS) for first- and second-level degrees (for degrees awarded in countries
participating in the Bologna Process);
▪ For degrees awarded in countries participating in the Bologna Process: Diploma Supplement (DS)
for first- and second-level degrees.
▪ For qualifications from the United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand: Higher Education
Achievement Report (HEAR), Australian Higher Education Graduation Statement (AHEGS),
Tertiary Education Qualification Statement (TEQS);
▪ For degrees obtained in China: CHSI verification report for the Bachelor’s degree (学信网：学位在
线验证报告或学位认证报告), CHSI verification report for the Official Transcript of Records (学信网：
成绩验证报告);
▪ For degrees obtained in France, in the case of attendance at a Grande École, the following must
be submitted: the complete Transcript of Records, including the two years of Classes
Préparatoires; the Certificate of Passing the Concours (entrance exam); and the Bachelor’s
Degree in the form of a DE – Diplôme d’établissement, issued exclusively by the institution and
certifying the completion of 180 ECTS credits;
▪ For degrees from countries where there is a distinction between academic qualifications and
vocational qualifications (e.g., the Netherlands, Switzerland, Finland, Germany), please note that
vocational qualifications are generally not considered eligible. Therefore, they will be evaluated
on a case-by-case basis depending on the country where the degree was obtained.
